input: n and k are integers with 2 <= n <= 9 and 0 <= k <= 9. Integer inputs are plain int values excluding bool. Containers are ordinary lists and strings are ordinary str values, without subclasses or overloaded behavior. No concurrent mutation or modified standard built-ins are allowed. Preconditions are not dynamically validated. Size bounds do not guarantee available memory or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: A fresh ascending list containing every n-digit positive integer whose neighboring decimal digits have absolute difference k, exactly once. No leading zero is allowed. For k=0 the repeated-digit values are not duplicated. Deterministic ordering: starting digits ascend from 1 to 9; for every prefix the next higher digit is expanded before the next lower digit. Breadth-level expansion therefore preserves the same fixed-depth leaf order as this ordered depth-first traversal.
mutation_aliasing: Only scalar inputs are read. Successive private prefix containers are replaced by new containers. The returned final container is independent of other calls and exposes no hidden shared state. The Solution instance retains no state; separate calls share no mutable result state.
numeric: A prefix has at most nine digits and is at most 999999999. Each accepted prefix*10+digit construction stays in that range; last-k and last+k are within [-9,18]. All arithmetic and modulo operations are exact safe-integer operations.
complexity: At most 9*2^(n-1) final branches and O(9*2^n) total prefix-processing/allocation work, with O(9*2^(n-1)) live storage including current and following levels and output. This is a conservative bound; digit-range checks and k=0 deduplication can greatly reduce it. Each transition is constant-time bounded integer arithmetic.
